findings.body: The new branch renders `TableWidgetVisualization` with a hardcoded empty `columns={[]}` and empty `tableData` instead of the actual `result`/`fields`/`eventView`, so the table displays no columns and no rows, dropping all query results.
findings.failure_mode: Users with the flag see blank tables; the widget silently loses its data.
findings.impact: The new branch renders `TableWidgetVisualization` with a hardcoded empty `columns={[]}` and empty `tableData` instead of the actual `result`/`fields`/`eventView`, so the table displays no columns and no rows, dropping all query results.
findings.root_cause: The feature-flagged replacement wires up placeholder empty literals rather than the widget's existing table data.
findings.suggested_fix: Pass the real data to `TableWidgetVisualization`: derive `columns` from `fields`/`fieldAliases` and map `result.data`/`result.meta` into the `tableData` prop instead of empty literals.
findings.title: Table widget renders empty columns and data, dropping query results

findings.verifier_reason: Patch lines 164-174 clearly show `TableWidgetVisualization` with hardcoded `columns={[]}` and `tableData={{data: [], meta: {fields: {}, units: {}}}}` - empty literals instead of actual data. This is a clear bug when feature flag is enabled.

raw_findings.root_cause: The refactor omitted the explicit react-query options that were present on the original useApiQuery call.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Preserve the previous options (staleTime:0, refetchOnWindowFocus:false, retry:false) on the new useQuery call unless intentionally changed.

raw_findings.failure_mode: Intended-hidden attributes leak into the default rendered list, defeating the purpose of the new HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES constant.
raw_findings.impact: The attributes 'is_segment', 'project_id', and 'received' remain visible in the default (unfiltered) view because the early return `if (!searchQuery.trim()) return sorted;` bypasses the HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES exclusion; they are only hidden once the user types a search query.
raw_findings.root_cause: The new HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES exclusion was added only inside the search-query filter branch, not the no-query return path.

validated_findings.verifier_reason: Patch lines 81-86 show `analytics.record` called at top of `post()` before the feature flag check at lines 88-91. This means analytics fires even for 404 responses when feature is disabled.

validated_findings.body: Validation passes even though neither timing field is present; the previous BrowserReport dataclass required timestamp, so this is a silent relaxation that allows reports with no timing information.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Missing timing data passes validation instead of being rejected.
validated_findings.impact: Validation passes even though neither timing field is present; the previous BrowserReport dataclass required timestamp, so this is a silent relaxation that allows reports with no timing information.
validated_findings.root_cause: Both age and timestamp were made required=False with only mutual-exclusion validators and no at-least-one enforcement.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Add a validate()/cross-field check requiring exactly one of age or timestamp to be present.
validated_findings.title: Browser report serializer accepts reports lacking both age and timestamp
validated_findings.trigger: A browser report payload is submitted that omits both the 'age' and 'timestamp' fields.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The validators `validate_timestamp` and `validate_age` only run when their respective fields are present. If both are absent, neither validator runs, so no mutual-exclusion error is raised. However, the claim about 'previous BrowserReport dataclass required timestamp' is unverified - no evidence of prior implementation shown. The relaxation may be intentional for spec compatibility.

validated_findings.body: The new branch renders `TableWidgetVisualization` with a hardcoded empty `columns={[]}` and empty `tableData` instead of the actual `result`/`fields`/`eventView`, so the table displays no columns and no rows, dropping all query results.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Users with the flag see blank tables; the widget silently loses its data.
validated_findings.impact: The new branch renders `TableWidgetVisualization` with a hardcoded empty `columns={[]}` and empty `tableData` instead of the actual `result`/`fields`/`eventView`, so the table displays no columns and no rows, dropping all query results.
validated_findings.root_cause: The feature-flagged replacement wires up placeholder empty literals rather than the widget's existing table data.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Pass the real data to `TableWidgetVisualization`: derive `columns` from `fields`/`fieldAliases` and map `result.data`/`result.meta` into the `tableData` prop instead of empty literals.
validated_findings.title: Table widget renders empty columns and data, dropping query results
validated_findings.trigger: An organization has the `use-table-widget-visualization` feature flag enabled and views a dashboard table widget that returns rows in `tableResults`.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Patch lines 164-174 clearly show `TableWidgetVisualization` with hardcoded `columns={[]}` and `tableData={{data: [], meta: {fields: {}, units: {}}}}` - empty literals instead of actual data. This is a clear bug when feature flag is enabled.

validated_findings.body: `fieldAlignment` receives the human-readable label (e.g. 'Count of Span Duration') rather than the field key, producing incorrect text alignment for numeric columns when no `type` is present.
validated_findings.evidence: const align = fieldAlignment(column.name, column.type as ColumnValueType);
validated_findings.failure_mode: Numeric columns render left-aligned instead of right-aligned.
validated_findings.impact: `fieldAlignment` receives the human-readable label (e.g. 'Count of Span Duration') rather than the field key, producing incorrect text alignment for numeric columns when no `type` is present.
validated_findings.root_cause: Passing the display name where the field identifier is expected.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Call `fieldAlignment(String(column.key), column.type as ColumnValueType)` so alignment is derived from the actual field key.
validated_findings.title: Header alignment computed from display name instead of field key
validated_findings.trigger: A column supplies a custom display `name` different from its `key` and omits `type` (e.g. custom columns in the spec/stories), so alignment falls back to name-based detection.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Patch line 35 shows `fieldAlignment(column.name, column.type as ColumnValueType)`. The claim assumes `column.name` is a display label vs `column.key`, but TabularColumn interface not fully shown. The `type` is passed, so alignment would use type when available. Impact is speculative.

validated_findings.body: `Boolean(normalizedDateRange)` is always true because `normalizeDateTimeParams` never returns a falsy value, so the guard adds no gating and misleads readers into thinking the query is conditionally disabled on the date range.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Dead condition gives false impression of conditional enabling.
validated_findings.impact: `Boolean(normalizedDateRange)` is always true because `normalizeDateTimeParams` never returns a falsy value, so the guard adds no gating and misleads readers into thinking the query is conditionally disabled on the date range.
validated_findings.root_cause: Guarding on a value that is unconditionally truthy.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Remove the `Boolean(normalizedDateRange)` term or replace it with a real condition (e.g. presence of a concrete start/end) if date gating was intended.
validated_findings.title: Redundant always-true enabled guard in useFeedbackSummary
validated_findings.trigger: Any render of the hook; `normalizeDateTimeParams` always returns an object.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The claim that `normalizeDateTimeParams` never returns falsy is plausible but not proven from context. The guard may be defensive coding or future-proofing. This is a code style/clarity issue, not a functional bug.

validated_findings.body: useTopEvents now returns TOP_EVENTS_LIMIT instead of undefined for multi-y-axis queries, so a top-N query is issued where it previously was disabled, contradicting the retained comment 'when there are no multiple y-axes chart' and potentially producing incorrect/failed series results.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Runtime query behavior diverges from intended semantics for multi-y-axis aggregate queries.
validated_findings.impact: useTopEvents now returns TOP_EVENTS_LIMIT instead of undefined for multi-y-axis queries, so a top-N query is issued where it previously was disabled, contradicting the retained comment 'when there are no multiple y-axes chart' and potentially producing incorrect/failed series results.
validated_findings.root_cause: The refactor from Visualize.yAxes[] to Visualize.yAxis dropped the multi-y-axis check entirely instead of translating it to visualizes.length > 1.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Reintroduce the guard adapted to the new model, e.g. return undefined when visualizes.length > 1 (multiple y-axes now map to multiple visualizes), and restore the visualizes input/dependency.
validated_findings.title: Removal of multi-y-axis guard enables top-N for multi-visualize queries
validated_findings.trigger: A user configures an aggregate-mode query with a group by and more than one y-axis (now represented as multiple Visualize objects, each with a single yAxis).
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Patch shows LEFT side line 28 had `if (visualizes.some(visualize => visualize.yAxes.length > 1))` check that returned undefined. This was removed in the patch (lines 28-30 deleted). The comment 'when there are no multiple y-axes chart' remains but the guard is gone, changing behavior.

validated_findings.body: Consumers relying on isLoading to distinguish the initial load will now see isLoading=true on every background refetch, causing loading UI to reappear where it previously did not.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Loading indicator semantics change for downstream components.
validated_findings.impact: Consumers relying on isLoading to distinguish the initial load will now see isLoading=true on every background refetch, causing loading UI to reappear where it previously did not.
validated_findings.root_cause: The migration from useApiQuery to useQuery repurposed isFetching for the previously returned initial-load isLoading value.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Map isLoading to the query's initial-load state (isPending/isLoading) rather than isFetching, keeping isFetching separate if needed.
validated_findings.title: isLoading now reflects isFetching, flagging loading on background refetches
validated_findings.trigger: Any background refetch of trace item attribute keys (e.g., page filter change) after the initial load has completed.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Patch line 61 shows `isLoading: isFetching`. The original code (LEFT side line 93) had `isLoading: result.isLoading`. `isFetching` is true during background refetches while `isLoading` is only true for initial load. This changes semantics for consumers.

validated_findings.body: Attribute key requests may now retry on error and refetch on window focus (unless overridden by global defaults), producing extra network requests compared to the prior explicit options.
validated_findings.impact: Attribute key requests may now retry on error and refetch on window focus (unless overridden by global defaults), producing extra network requests compared to the prior explicit options.
validated_findings.root_cause: The refactor omitted the explicit react-query options that were present on the original useApiQuery call.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Preserve the previous options (staleTime:0, refetchOnWindowFocus:false, retry:false) on the new useQuery call unless intentionally changed.
validated_findings.title: Dropped query options (retry/refetchOnWindowFocus/staleTime) change fetch behavior
validated_findings.trigger: The attribute keys request errors, or the window regains focus, after the migration to useQuery which no longer specifies retry:false, refetchOnWindowFocus:false, staleTime:0.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Patch lines 50-54 show new `useQuery` call without explicit `retry`, `refetchOnWindowFocus`, `staleTime` options. However, these may be set by global defaults or intentionally changed. The impact is speculative without knowing the global config.

validated_findings.body: The attributes 'is_segment', 'project_id', and 'received' remain visible in the default (unfiltered) view because the early return `if (!searchQuery.trim()) return sorted;` bypasses the HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES exclusion; they are only hidden once the user types a search query.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Intended-hidden attributes leak into the default rendered list, defeating the purpose of the new HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES constant.
validated_findings.impact: The attributes 'is_segment', 'project_id', and 'received' remain visible in the default (unfiltered) view because the early return `if (!searchQuery.trim()) return sorted;` bypasses the HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES exclusion; they are only hidden once the user types a search query.
validated_findings.root_cause: The new HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES exclusion was added only inside the search-query filter branch, not the no-query return path.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Apply the `!HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES.includes(attribute.name)` exclusion to the unfiltered `sorted` result as well (e.g. filter out hidden attributes before the `!searchQuery.trim()` early return), so hidden attributes are excluded in both branches.
validated_findings.title: Hidden attributes only filtered when a search query is present
validated_findings.trigger: View the EAP span attributes drawer with no text typed into the attribute search box.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Patch lines 61-68 show early return `if (!searchQuery.trim()) return sorted;` at line 62, then HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES filter only applied inside the else branch (lines 65-68). Hidden attributes are not filtered when searchQuery is empty.

validated_findings.body: The removed `Container` was `styled(FlexBox)` which supplied `align-items: center` and `gap: ${space(1)}`; the replacement `<Flex justify="space-between">` omits both, so the tabs and TraceContextVitals are no longer vertically centered nor gapped, changing the layout.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Visual regression: misaligned/ungapped trace tabs row.
validated_findings.impact: The removed `Container` was `styled(FlexBox)` which supplied `align-items: center` and `gap: ${space(1)}`; the replacement `<Flex justify="space-between">` omits both, so the tabs and TraceContextVitals are no longer vertically centered nor gapped, changing the layout.
validated_findings.root_cause: Migration to the Flex component dropped the align-items and gap properties that were inherited from the previous styled FlexBox/Container.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Add `align="center"` (and `gap={space(1)}` if the original spacing is desired) to the replacement `<Flex>` to preserve the previous `Container`/`FlexBox` styling.
validated_findings.title: Trace tabs container loses vertical centering and gap after Flex migration
validated_findings.trigger: Render TraceTabsAndVitals in the non-loading, non-error state.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Patch line 93 shows `<Flex ref={setRef} justify="space-between">` replacing `<Container ref={setRef}>`. The claim about missing `align-items: center` and `gap` requires knowing the deleted Container's styles, which aren't shown in patch. The Flex component may have different defaults.

validated_findings.body: The removed `FlexBox` set `flex-grow: 1` plus `height: 100%`; the replacement `<Flex direction="column" flex={1}>` sets `flex: 1 1 0%` but no longer applies `height: 100%`, which can alter the waterfall container's vertical sizing.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Potential layout/height regression of the trace waterfall panel.
validated_findings.impact: The removed `FlexBox` set `flex-grow: 1` plus `height: 100%`; the replacement `<Flex direction="column" flex={1}>` sets `flex: 1 1 0%` but no longer applies `height: 100%`, which can alter the waterfall container's vertical sizing.
validated_findings.root_cause: The Flex replacement omitted the `height: 100%` rule present in the deleted FlexBox styled component.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Preserve the previous sizing by adding an explicit height (e.g. `height="100%"` or equivalent style) to the replacement `<Flex>`, matching the removed FlexBox's `height: 100%`.
validated_findings.title: TraceWaterfall wrapper loses height:100% after Flex migration
validated_findings.trigger: Render the TraceWaterfall component in any layout.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Patch line 712 shows `<Flex direction="column" flex={1}>`. The claim about missing `height: 100%` requires knowing the deleted FlexBox's styles. The `flex={1}` may provide equivalent sizing in flex context. Impact is speculative.

validated_findings.body: TypeScript/bundler resolves `Flex` as undefined, producing a compile error or a runtime `Flex is not defined` when the audit log list renders.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Module fails to compile or throws at render because the referenced symbol is unbound.
validated_findings.impact: TypeScript/bundler resolves `Flex` as undefined, producing a compile error or a runtime `Flex is not defined` when the audit log list renders.
validated_findings.root_cause: The refactor swapped the local FlexCenter styled component for the shared Flex component but omitted the corresponding import statement.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Add `import {Flex} from 'sentry/components/core/layout';` to the imports of auditLogList.tsx, mirroring the import additions made in codeOwnerFileTable.tsx and instanceLevelOAuthDetails.tsx.
validated_findings.title: auditLogList uses <Flex> without adding the required import
validated_findings.trigger: Building/rendering AuditLogList after FlexCenter was replaced by the Flex component, when Flex was not already imported into this module (the styled FlexCenter previously stood in for it and no import hunk is present in the patch).
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Patch line 368 shows `<Flex align="center">` replacing `<FlexCenter>`. The patch shows this is a refactor from styled component to Flex. The import of Flex would need to be verified, but the patch doesn't show the imports section. Without seeing missing import, cannot confirm compile error.

validated_findings.body: The former `flex: 1` set flex-basis:0% so the column shared space independent of content; `grow={1}` only sets flex-grow with flex-basis:auto, so the column sizes from its content and can push/overflow the Metadata column, changing the layout.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Visual/layout regression that is not caught because behavior differs only under content-width pressure.
validated_findings.impact: The former `flex: 1` set flex-basis:0% so the column shared space independent of content; `grow={1}` only sets flex-grow with flex-basis:auto, so the column sizes from its content and can push/overflow the Metadata column, changing the layout.
validated_findings.root_cause: Translating `flex: 1` to `grow={1}` drops the flex-basis:0% component of the shorthand.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Ensure the Flex.Item also zeroes the basis (e.g. use the equivalent of `flex: 1`/basis:0) rather than only setting grow, or keep the previous `flex: 1` styling.
validated_findings.title: Flex.Item grow={1} does not reproduce `flex: 1` sizing
validated_findings.trigger: Rendering the integration InformationCard where the description column contains wide content next to the Metadata column.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Patch line 247 shows `<Flex.Item grow={1}>`. The claim about `flex: 1` vs `grow={1}` difference is technically correct (flex-basis differs), but the actual visual impact depends on content and container. This is a potential subtle layout change, not a clear bug.
